newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Goldman sees Philippine peso depreciating.
newsitem.headline: Goldman sees Philippine peso depreciating.

text.p: U.S.-based investment firm Goldman Sachs has projected the Philippine peso to depreciate to 26.4 against the dollar by year end and to 27.3 by fourth quarter 1997.

This would be brought about by the combined effects of the country's widening trade deficit and an anticipated deceleration of the inflation rate, Goldman said in its October report released by Philippine officials to reporters at the weekend.
The peso ended weaker in heavy trading on Friday at 26.280 from 26.265.
Goldman said the peso was currently "overvalued" by one percent relative to the exchange rate with the dollar.
"We expect modest depreciation of the peso to 26.4 pesos per $1 by yearend and 27.3 pesos per $1 on a 12-month horizon," it said.

It said a widening trade gap would raise more demand for dollars, causing the peso to weaken. With an ancipated decline in the inflation rate, interest rates based on the bellwether 91-day treasury bill would continue to drop, resulting in a slowdown in the supply of dollars in the form of portfolio investments.

Philippine officials have projected the country's trade gap to hit $14 billion next year from $12 billion this year. The inflation rate fell to 4.4 percent year-on-year in September and from 7.9 percent in August.
